question.text: An AMC decides to change the benchmark index of one of its equity schemes from Nifty 50 TRI to Nifty 100 TRI. Which statement best reflects the source-backed treatment of this change?

answer.text: Benchmark changes may be made by the AMC in consultation with the trustees and the change must be justified and documented
Is a routine operational change that requires no communication to unitholders
Requires SEBI to personally approve the new benchmark before implementation
Automatically converts the scheme from a large-cap to a multi-cap category

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook states that AMCs can change the scheme's benchmark in consultation with the trustees and that the change must be justified and documented. The source does not, on its own, treat a benchmark change as automatically triggering the fundamental-attribute exit framework, so the safest source-backed description is that the trustees are consulted and the rationale is recorded. The Trap: Benchmark changes are not just internal paperwork; they must be justified and documented, and trustees must be consulted. SEBI does not personally approve individual benchmark choices, and changing the benchmark does not by itself reclassify the scheme into a different SEBI category. Note: Pair benchmark changes with the trustees-plus-documentation requirement. Treat any fundamental-attribute exit treatment as a separate question that requires its own specific source.
